parts.message:
**Not landing the coalesce work.** Its own report contains the sentence that kills it:

> Actual independent providers can overwrite SQL rows while the old orchestrator waits for an ACK, so old bounded queries already skip many intermediate versions.

The existing re-query design *already* coalesces. Re-reading the current row, rather than replaying each version, is the coalescing. Adding `Stream.aggregate` on top buys nothing, and the report admits it "may perform more eager reads while an ACK is held". Net-negative complexity, and its own test passes identically against HEAD.

The investigation was still worth it. It produced the finding that matters: **coalescing frequency can't fix the asymptotics at all**. A response that runs T seconds sends T/window deliveries of O(T) bytes each, so it stays quadratic no matter how wide the window. Only sending the suffix instead of the whole row makes it linear.

Let me check the ni8.24 P1's real shape before I brief the delta.

parts.message:
[01:07:02] Session-convergence explorer landed, and it found the thing that decides whether 2D is buildable as stated: **`SessionInfo` is not a projection of `SessionRow` — it's a join.** Five of its ten fields don't come from the read model at all.

| `SessionInfo` field | actual source |
|---|---|
| `processing` | status poller's in-memory map — *not* `row.status`, which the adapter drops |
| `pendingQuestionCount` | session-manager in-memory state |
| `forkPointTimestamp` | fork metadata; **no column backs it** |
| `parentID`, `forkMessageId` | row columns, with a fork-metadata fallback |

The shell subscription streams rows out of the event store, so it structurally cannot produce those fields. That's the crux of Round 3, and whether the clean answer exists depends on one fact I don't have yet — whether `status`, pending-question counts, and fork-point timestamps have event sources the projector could write. `status` *is* already a column the projector writes (`session-projector.ts:118`); the adapter just ignores it in favour of the poller. Explorer running on exactly that.[01:08:02] ## Round 3 (partial — the rest waits on two running explorers)

**1. Fork — what happens to the unary `ListSessions`.** It has exactly two callers: initial load in `ChatLayout.svelte:344-352` (a `Promise.all` of `roots:true` and `roots:false`), and sidebar remote search in `SessionList.svelte:103-113`, debounced 300ms. The subscription's snapshot covers the first. The second is the only job the RPC does that a snapshot+delta stream doesn't — and the server-side filter it exists for is just `session.title` and `session.id` (`ws-rpc.ts:855-858`).

| # | Option | Trade-off |
|---|---|---|
| **A** ★ | **Delete it.** The snapshot hands the client every session, so search becomes a client-side filter on `title`+`id` — precisely what the server matches today | Deletes the remote-search path, the debounce, the `search: true` store arm and the dual `roots` calls in one go; the store already 
…
 frontend keeps `rootSessions` and `allSessions` as separate arrays fed by two RPC calls. One subscription carries all sessions and the store derives roots by `parentID`, which `handleSessionList` already does in its untagged branch (`session.svelte.ts:311-320`).

Still out: the in-memory-fields fork (blocked on whether `status`, pending-question counts and fork timestamps can be projected), plus the reducer/store seam, which arms of `ws-dispatch` die, and where the exactly-once assertion lives.

## Goal

Implement a `ProjectRegistry` class that replaces three independent data structures (`projects` Map, `projectRelays` Map, `pendingRelaySlugs` Set) on the Daemon class with a single class using a discriminated union type. This eliminates a race condition that caused a forever-loading screen on phones (browser loads page because project exists in `projects` Map, but WebSocket upgrade is silently rejected because relay doesn't exist yet in `projectRelays` Map).

## Instructions

- Follow TDD approach with `pnpm check`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm test:unit` for verification
- Pre-commit hooks run build + lint + test automatically
- The project uses Svelte 5, TypeScript, Vitest, Biome linter
- **DO NOT modify existing icon files** (`apple-touch-icon.png`, `web-app-manifest-*.png`, `favicon-*.png`)
- **The Edit and Write tools HANG on this codebase** — use `bash` with `python3` or `cat` for ALL file edits
- The user wants "the best testing possible" — property-based tests, stateful model tests, and comprehensive unit tests
- The user wants maximum type strictness to prevent bugs
- The design doc lives at `docs/plans/2026-03-13-project-registry-design.md`
- The implementation plan lives at `docs/plans/2026-03-13-project-registry-implementation.md` (2020 lines)
- Using **Subagent-Driven Development** skill for execution — fresh subagent per task, spec review + code quality review after each

## Discoveries

### Root cause of the forever-loading bug
The HTTP router checks `this.projects` Map to serve index.html for `/p/{slug}/`. The WS upgrade handler checks `this.projectRelays` Map to accept WebSocket connections. During the window between project registration and relay creation, browsers load the page but WebSocket upgrades are silently rejected. The `ProjectRegistry` eliminates this with `waitForRelay()` — a promise-based approach using EventEmitter events.

Good question. The idiomatic Svelte approach is `{#key}` blocks with `in:/out:` transitions. Instead of swapping text in-place on a GPU-cached element (which is what causes the WebKit issue), Svelte **destroys the old element and creates a new one**. Each element only ever has one text value, so there's never a stale GPU cache to invalidate.

This would replace all the manual `transitionend` / `visibility` / `animation pause` / `tick()` / `rAF` machinery with about 5 lines of Svelte.

## CCS Provider Routing — Investigation Complete

**Key finding from `getClaudeEnvVars()` in `env-builder.ts`:**

```typescript
ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL: `http://127.0.0.1:${port}/api/provider/${provider}`
```

**How it works:**
- CCS CLIProxy serves all providers on **one port** via path-based routing
- Each provider gets its own endpoint: `/api/provider/claude`, `/api/provider/gemini`, `/api/provider/codex`, etc.
- The `extractProviderFromPathname()` function parses the provider from the URL path
- `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` (not `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`) is set to CCS's internal API key (`getEffectiveApiKey()`)

**Answer to the open question:** Setting `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` to `/api/provider/claude/v1` gives OpenCode access to **only Claude** through that CCS instance. To access Gemini, you'd need `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:{port}/api/provider/gemini`. Each provider URL is a different path on the same port.

**However**, CCS also supports a **composite/root endpoint** (no `/api/provider/` path) where routing is based on the model name in the request body. This is used for composite tiers where different model tiers (opus/sonnet/haiku) map to different providers.

**Implication for opencode-relay:**
- For a single provider per instance: `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:{port}/api/provider/{provider}`
- For multi-provider (model-based routing): `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:{port}` (root URL, CCS routes by model name)
- `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` (not `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`) should be set to CCS's API key

**Important correction to my earlier design:** The env var is `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`, not `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`. And the URL path does NOT have `/v1` — it's just `/api/provider/{provider}`.
